notes: Architectural adherence: The event bus is used correctly for task.assigned and task.statusChanged, but the comment.added handler in NotificationService is a stub that does nothing ('we just log'), which breaks the notification contract for comments. More critically, the router directly calls taskService.getById() before creating a comment (to fetch the task title), which is a cross-service data read leaking into the routing layer — a workaround for not being able to pass context via events. The router correctly imports all services and acts as the sole HTTP handler. Completeness: All five services exist. User CRUD is complete. Project CRUD plus add/remove members is present. Task CRUD, assign, and status change are implemented. Comment create/get-by-task/get-by-id/delete are present. NotificationService has getByUser and markAsRead. The demo exercises most flows. However: (1) GET /tasks without projectId returns 400 instead of returning all tasks — limiting usability. (2) The comment.added notification is explicitly not implemented, so the notification service only reacts to two of the three required events. (3) DELETE /users/:id returns 204 with a JSON body (null), which is incorrect HTTP semantics — 204 must have no body. Same issue for DELETE /projects and DELETE /tasks. (4) No input validation (missing required fields, invalid status values not in the enum, duplicate emails). Code quality: TypeScript types are clean, interfaces are well-defined, Map-based stores are appropriate, error handling in the router is reasonable, the event bus error isolation (try/catch per subscriber) is good practice, code is readable and consistently structured. Constraint compliance: (1) No external npm dependencies — satisfied. (2) Each service in its own file — satisfied. (3) HTTP handling only in router — mostly satisfied, but router reaches into taskService to resolve task title before comment creation, which is a mild violation of service boundary encapsulation. (4) Event bus used for inter-service communication — partially violated because the comment.added notification is a no-op stub, meaning the notification service silently ignores that event. (5) Forward-only status transitions — correctly implemented with index comparison. (6) Each service owns its own data store — satisfied.
